column1: # Classes for scripts/measure/tuple-replay.sh: every row whose verdict,
# prescriptions or record moved between a baseline and this revision.
# The first line whose two expressions match names the row. A move that loosens
# a verdict (deny to pass or allow) is named by its own line before the
# general ones, with the reason it is right.

column5: npm reads an option it does not define, with no `=value`, as a Boolean (nopt), so its command is `x`, an alias of exec, and the package it runs is `exec`: evil@1.0.0 is that program's argument and is never fetched

column3: ^npm (-x user@example\.com|--cache-dir 'a b'|--filter "a b"|--cwd=x@y|--with x) install evil@1\.0\.0$
column5: npm reads the word after an option it does not define as its command (nopt; `--cwd` expands to the shorthands `-c -w -d`, ending in the command `info`), so npm runs no install: it errors on an unknown command, or with `--with x` runs `npm x` (exec) on the package `install`; the gate reads it the same way

npx and nopt read `--cwd` as the shorthands `--call --workspace --loglevel info`: the command is `info` and npm runs the package `info`; the deny it had came from the landing reading `--cwd` as a directory npm never uses
`x@y` is the value of the option word `--install-dir=x@y`, not a package; the deny named a package that is never installed
`out@1.0.0` is the target of a redirection, the shell's, not an operand; the deny named a package that is never installed

an unpinned npm alias installs its target, evil-pkg, with no version to check; the deny prescribed `left-pad@npm`, which names no package and could never approve, so it is recorded as evil-pkg instead

bunx reads `--cwd` as a switch (bun 1.4.2, measured by scripts/measure/manager-option-reading.sh), so the word after it is the package bunx fetches and runs, and evil@1.0.0 is that program's argument; the gate records that package and no longer checks an argument nothing fetches
text the shell only prints or quotes (`echo 'sh -c "pip install ..."'`) is data, and an escaped-quote decoy closes before the install; neither runs an install

column1: # --- Records the npm CLI install leaves to the PostToolUse hook -----------------

column5: an npm CLI install is read by the effect gate where it leaves a trace, and its record is the PostToolUse hook's (no install trace, or global); the pre-guard no longer writes one for it

column1: # --- Records bun's own command choice adds ------------------------------------

column5: bun takes for its command the first word that does not start with `-` (bun 1.4.2, measured by scripts/measure/manager-option-reading.sh), so `bun <option> x add ...` runs `bun x add ...`, which fetches the package `add` with no pin; the record now names it, and the install reading is still judged

column1: # --- Prescriptions that now name the package installed --------------------------

column5: the prescription named a token that is no package (an option, its value, a redirection target, a truncated name, an alias name), or missed the package; it now names what the manager installs, read with that manager's own grammar
a pinned install the gate did not read (an alias, a runner, a create, an option before the command, a version flag, quoting, a backslash, an npm 10 option) is now checked
an install of a package with no pin was not recorded, or recorded without naming it (main wrote the command only); the record now names each unpinned operand

the record named a word that is no package, or an extra one (an option's value, a runner's program argument, a local Go package, the lexer's blank mark, a version flag's value, an option before the command); it now names only the operands the manager installs
an npm install the gate did not recognize (npm link, an install in a payload, an option before the command) is now read and made inert
the deny came from an unread landing (a directory the gate looked in that npm never uses) and named no package; it now names the package
